result.description:
Commercial Electrician required for local Mackay projects!    Your new company  
 Our client is a well-established, family-owned electrical business experiencing continued growth across Mackay and the Whitsundays. With a strong focus on team culture, safety, and quality workmanship, they pride themselves on creating a supportive environment where employees are genuinely valued, and long-term careers are encouraged. 
  Your new role  
 This role will see you completing a variety of domestic and commercial electrical works across the Mackay and Whitsundays regions. You'll work as part of a close-knit team, delivering high-quality electrical solutions while enjoying flexible hours that allow you to prioritise family and personal commitments. This is a stable, long-term opportunity within a growing business. 
  What you'll need to succeed  
 
 
 Licensed Fitter Mechanic (Electrical) qualification 
 
 
 
 
 QLD Electrical licence 
 
 
 
 
 Experience in commercial electrical work (preferred) 
 
 
 
 
 Strong reliability and motivation 
 
 
 
 
 Ability to work independently and as part of a team 
 
 
 
 
 Commitment to safety and quality workmanship 
 
 
  What you'll get in return  
 In return, you'll receive an excellent hourly rate of $60 per hour plus penalties and bonuses, along with a company vehicle and iPad/phone. Flexible working arrangements are available, as well as ongoing training and development opportunities. Most importantly, you'll be joining a supportive, family-oriented business that values work-life balance and offers long-term job security. 
  What you need to do now  
 If you're interested in this role, applications can be submitted via the "apply now" button. Please ensure you are submitting an up-to-date CV. If you have any further questions, please contact Mika Nuttall on (07) 4960 1128. 
 If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.  Please  click here  to apply.

Exciting fulltime opportunity
Salary: $105,000 to $110,000 + Super
BIBO/DIDO roster of 2:2 OR FIFO roster of 2:1
Location - Multiple sites across Queensland & NSW

For the Love of Food! Join the Sodexo team
Do you want to be part of one of the country’s largest and most diverse Chef Teams?

Sodexo inspires and nurtures our chefs to become leaders in their industry and deliver fantastic food which delights our customers. All we ask is that you have a passion for what you do and an eye for innovation.

If you’re looking to be part of a team driving the latest food trends across Australia, we have various permanent opportunities available for suitably experienced & qualified Chefs (Cert III Commercial Cookery equivalent) working either a BIBO/DIDO roster of 2:2 or FIFO roster of 2:1 out of Brisbane; and FIFO rosters of 2:1 out of the Cairns, Darwin & Townsville regions within our Energy & Resources portfolio.

Who are we looking for?
If you have a passion for food, thrive in fast-paced environments delivering food to the highest standards, have strong interpersonal skills and love working alongside a team, we want you! To be successful, you’ll need:
• Australian Citizenship or Full Australian working rights OR have relevant Energy & Resources Chef experience, be currently residing in Australia & seeking Visa sponsorship
• Trade Certificate, Certificate III in Commercial Cookery
• Previous experience in mass-catering environments (volume cooking)
• A strong understanding of food hygiene, safety and cleanliness (Food Safety Supervisor Certificate highly regarded at line Chef level and a must for Leadership roles)
• Strong cooking and food preparation skills including knife skills are essential
• Flexibility to work a variety of rosters and shifts

Why choose Sodexo?
Sodexo is the world’s leading provider of food services. We have a well-respected culinary history – demonstrated by our Love of Food. How do we offer world-class food? We start by attracting top culinary talent. Our chefs are at the heart of what we do, and we are committed to providing opportunities for chefs who are as passionate about food as we are.
Working with Sodexo is more than a job; it’s a chance to be part of something greater because we believe our everyday actions have a big impact. With us, you belong in a company that allows you to act with purpose and thrive in your own way. We are always looking for people to join our team and help us create a lasting impact on individuals, society, and the planet.
At Sodexo, we are a proud Equal Opportunity Employer and encourage applications from all applicants regardless of age, race, sex, ethnicity, religion and beliefs and people with disabilities.
We offer a competitive salary, many training, upskilling and development opportunities and an outstanding benefits and recognition program!

How to apply?
If you are interested in joining the Sodexo team and meet the minimum criteria outlined above, please apply with your resume detailing relevant employment experience and availability.
One of our friendly recruiters will contact shortlisted candidates for a phone interview. This is also your opportunity to ask any questions you may have.
What are you waiting for? Submit your application today and become part of the Sodexo family!

About the role
We are seeking a Leading Hand Tradesperson with a minimum of 4 years experience to join our family friendly team on the central Gold Coast, QLD. This full-time role is a hands on position for a skilled professional to contribute to the delivery of high-quality landscaping services for our diverse range of clients. As part of this role you will be involved in all aspects of soft and hard landscaping elements as well as high end maintenance, ensuring our projects are completed to the highest standard.

What you'll be doing
Undertaking landscaping tasks such as garden preparation, planting, mulching, and lawn installation and maintenance
Operating and maintaining landscaping equipment and tools in a safe and efficient manner
Implementing a diverse range of projects including paving, decking, retaining walls, stonework, irrigation and water features
Collaborating with the project team to ensure the successful delivery of landscaping projects
Managing and providing on site training for other staff.
Providing excellent customer service and communicating effectively with clients
Adhering to all relevant health, safety, and environmental regulations
Participating in ongoing training and development to enhance your skills and knowledge

What we're looking for
Minimum 4 years of experience in a similar role.
Able to work from plans and specifications.
Strong practical skills in all aspects of soft and hard landscaping.
Proficiency in the use of landscaping tools and equipment, skid steer loader and mini excavator with a commitment to safety.
Excellent attention to detail and the ability to work to high standards
Effective communication and customer service skills
A positive, proactive, and team-oriented attitude
A current car licence (C class) and access to reliable transportation
Must be an Australian citizen with legal work authorisation

About the Department - Program 






Partner Application Services is part of Digital & Information Division, and supports business-critical applications into a single, accountable function focused on reliability, lifecycle management, and high quality service delivery. The team provides system administration capability, consistent and dependable standards-aligned support. The department's role is to deliver efficient and continuously improving application services that meet changing organisational and customer needs.







About the Role 






Join our team as a System Administrator on a full time, ongoing role to work at Scoresby and is based at Scoresby. In this role, you will be guided under the leadership of the Head of Partner Applications and working with the broader Partner Applications team. 






Explanation of the role and the projects-tasks (refer to full detail in the position description) 









The position of HMS & Smart Health System Support Officer (Full Time) is part of the Partner Applications team. The role will be 35 hours per week for HMS and 5 hours per week with Smart Health. 












The System Support Officer's role is to provide application support of Health Management System (HMS) and Smart Health to the business. 






The System Administrator Support Officer will provide a secure and stable IT environment, thus ensuring HMS & Smart Health delivers an integrated client management system within Monash Health Community. 




Additional responsibilities include consultation and development between stakeholders as well as other business units to improve integration and workflows with other departments within Monash Health.


Requirement to travel to other sites, hybrid working arrangement, Monday - Fridays, rotating on call roster. 








About You 






To be successful in this healthcare role, you will bring the following demonstrated skills, experience, and attributes: 










Reactive maintenance or 'break-fix' is required when an issue or outage has been reported.




Preventative maintenance is required for planning, testing and implementation of IT specific updates and othet maintenance as required.










Ability to create and update appropriate documentation, log Central and vendor calls, set up new access accounts, 




Liaise with Monash Health employees on usage of HMS application


Proficiency in SQL required to create scripts and generate custom reports using Microsoft SQL Server Management. 


Understand and carry out compliance and improvement against the key elements of quality and safety







Mandatory requirements of the role - qualifications, licences, memberships, 









Bachelor's degree in computer science, IT, or a related field preferred.












Prior experience in a system administrator role or similar.







For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to:


Liz Feeny, Head of Partner Applications, Digital & Information Division on M 0412 032 226

Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 







Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 







You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 







We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time.
